ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, the turns ratio of the primary to secondary coils of an ideal transformer is 4:1. A resistor $R_{1}$ with a resistance of $100\Omega$ is connected in the primary coil circuit, and a resistor $R_{2}$ with a resistance of $7.5\Omega$ is connected in the secondary coil circuit. The input terminal of the primary coil is connected to an AC power source with a voltage of $u=220\sqrt{2}\sin100\pi t(\mathrm{V})$. All meters are ideal meters.

1. The effective value of the power supply output voltage
2. The magnitude of the current reading $I_{1}$ and the magnitude of the voltage reading $U_{2}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the turns ratio of the primary to secondary coils of an ideal transformer is 4:1. A resistor $R_{1}$ with a resistance of $100\Omega$ is connected in the primary coil circuit, and a resistor $R_{2}$ with a resistance of $7.5\Omega$ is connected in the secondary coil circuit. The input terminal of the primary coil is connected to an AC power source with a voltage of $u=220\sqrt{2}\sin100\pi t(\mathrm{V})$. All meters are ideal meters. 1. The effective value of the power supply output voltage 2. The magnitude of the current reading $I_{1}$ and the magnitude of the voltage reading $U_{2}$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure, the AC power supply “~u” is connected into the primary-coil circuit; in the primary-coil circuit, ammeter A is connected in series with resistor R1, and then connected to the transformer primary coil. On the right side is the secondary-coil circuit, resistor R2 is connected between the upper and lower ends of the secondary coil, and voltmeter V is connected in parallel with this secondary-side port, so the voltmeter reading is the secondary-side terminal voltage. The problem statement explains that the meters are all ideal meters, so the ammeter can be regarded as zero resistance, and the voltmeter can be regarded as an open circuit, not changing the secondary-side load. Then reason: the power-supply voltage is u = 220√2 sin(100πt) V, and the effective value of a sinusoidal alternating current is equal to the peak value divided by √2, so the effective value of the power-supply output voltage is 220 V. The turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of the ideal transformer is Np:Ns = 4:1. The actual load on the secondary side is R2 = 7.5 Ω; referred to the primary side: R2' = (Np/Ns)^2 R2 = 4^2 × 7.5 Ω = 120 Ω. In the primary-side circuit, R1 = 100 Ω is in series with the referred load R2', so the total equivalent resistance seen by the power supply is 100 Ω + 120 Ω = 220 Ω. The ammeter reading is I1 = 220 V / 220 Ω = 1 A. The voltage across the primary coil, that is, the voltage on the referred load, is I1 × R2' = 1 A × 120 Ω = 120 V. The voltage ratio of an ideal transformer is Up:Us = Np:Ns = 4:1, so the secondary-side voltage Us = 120 V / 4 = 30 V. The voltmeter is connected in parallel at the secondary-side port, therefore U2 = 30 V.
